name: @visuelconcept/wui-para
title: Parametrization (PARA)
description: PARA datapoint-parametrization page (/para): two tabs — a nested DP-type model editor (create/change/delete types in place) and an instances/values browser (live values + config attributes). Embeds a proposal-only AI assistant (via the /api/ai bridge) and DPL ASCII import/export (multi-select DP/DPT) through the dplAscii MSA manager (WCCOAasciiSQLite). Engineering ops via the /api/para API.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-camera-streams
title: Camera Streams (RTSP)
description: View RTSP IP cameras in-browser (JSMpeg) over a same-origin ws relay to the rtspProxy manager (ffmpeg pulls each stream once and fans MPEG1-TS out to N clients).

name: @visuelconcept/wui-audit-trail
title: Audit Trail
description: Audit Trail page — pivot table of a datapoint's NGA-archived element history, with a config popup (DP/period/columns/refresh) persisted to an AuditTrail_Config DP.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-mosaic
title: Mosaic
description: Mosaic page — free drag/resize display wall embedding other dashboard views as chromeless same-origin iframes; 1 DP per board (Mosaic_Board) + an overview list.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-ampere
title: Ampère (electrical)
description: Ampère pages (/ampere + /ampere/:networkid) — draw single-line (mono-filaire) electrical distribution networks (TGBT/switchboards, disconnectors, breakers, busbars, transformers…) incl. railway electrification (catenary, track return, rectifier, sectioning switch, autotransformer, train) with an in-place edit mode, an IEC 60617 symbol toolbox, free per-device DP binding, live wire energisation by graph traversal through closed switchgear, free/attached live measurement labels, and a proposal-only AI assistant that generates network models. Stored as Ampere_Network DPs. The ampereSim JavaScript manager creates and drives the shared AmpereSim_Demo datapoint that every showcase binds to (live switchgear + measurement animation).

name: @visuelconcept/wui-report-builder
title: Report Builder
description: Report Builder pages (/report-builder + /report-builder/:reportid) — report instances from templates: fill data, recompute dataset aggregations from archives, checklist-gated multi-level signing, lock + print. Stored as ReportBuilder_Report DPs.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-report-templates
title: Report Templates
description: Report Templates page (/report-templates) — configurable templates (parameterised sections: text/comment/fields/table/DP-dataset+aggregation/checklist + multi-level signature workflow). Stored as ReportBuilder_Template DPs. Bundles the shared report-builder code it reuses.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-fleet-closures
title: Fleet Closures
description: Fleet Closures page (/fleet-closures) — manage non-working days (year/atelier/machine filters, JSON import-export, overlap replace/ignore/cancel).

name: @visuelconcept/wui-fleet-stop-analysis
title: Fleet Stop-Cause Analysis
description: Fleet Stop-Cause Analysis page (/fleet-stops) — downtime decomposition (dpGetPeriod + interval algorithm), table + echarts tabs.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-thermal-reports
title: Thermal Treatment Reports
description: Thermal Treatment Reports page (/thermal-reports) — per-charge heat-treatment reports, recipe paliers + tolerance band vs actual furnace temp curve (dpGetPeriod), quality/conformity, echarts band chart + print. 1 DP per report.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-fleet-kpi-analysis
title: Fleet KPI Analysis
description: Fleet KPI Analysis page (/fleet-kpi) — availability/TRS per machine over opening time minus closures, echarts; live per-machine TRS computed by the kpiCalc manager.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-production-orders
title: Production Orders
description: Production Orders page (/production-orders) — manage OF stored as a single JSON-list DP (ProductionOrders_List), CRUD + status workflow + echarts Gantt + fleet link; top-page KPIs computed server-side by the productionOrdersKpi manager (ProductionOrders_Kpi DP).

name: @visuelconcept/wui-remote-vnc
title: Remote VNC
description: Remote VNC page (/remote-vnc) — manage VNC connections (1 DP each) and open them in-browser with bundled noVNC over a same-origin /api/vnc/ws WebSocket↔TCP relay to the vncProxy manager (resolves id → host:port from RemoteVnc_ DPs).

name: @visuelconcept/wui-machine-fleet-3d
title: Machine Fleet
description: Machine Fleet 3D hub page (/machine-fleet-3d) — three.js 3D fleet view with per-machine state/KPI bubbles, stop-cause catalog, contextual machine dashboard (Gantt + Pareto), and an AI assistant. Managers: machineSim (fleet simulation), kpiCalc (live KPIs), aiAssistant (the AI assistant, via the /api/ai bridge). The assistant's MCP tools are provided by an OPTIONAL external WinCC OA MCP server (ETM @etm-professional-control/winccoa-mcp-server, ISC) — installed separately, not shipped here. AI provider tokens are read from the AI_Assistant_Config DP — NONE are shipped.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-process-monitor
title: Process Monitor
description: Process Monitor page (/process-monitor) — pmon manager console with one tab per connected server (distributed via per-system ProcessMonitor_Node DPs): status + start/stop/restart + restart-all, add/remove pmon configuration entries (SINGLE_MGR:INS/DEL, persisted to config/progs), plus project ZIP upload/deploy across all servers (optional folder purge, 7-Zip extraction into non-protected folders, config.env, optional restart) with GxP audit-trail tracing (session user). Bridged via /api/process-monitor to the processMonitor MSA manager (per-system agent + aggregator). Sensitive routes are role-gated server-side (Application Security roles 'control'/'edit-managers'/'deploy' — open until groups are assigned). DPL import handled elsewhere.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-app-security
title: Application Security
description: Application Security page (/app-security) — discover the roles each page module expects (declared in one AppSecurity_<module> DP per module: the module writes .roles, this page writes .assignments) and map every role to WinCC OA user groups. Open by default: a role with no group stays open to all connected users. Pages gate their UI live via the wui-kit hasRole$ primitive; sensitive backend routes enforce the same rules server-side (requireRole guard). /api/app-security resolves the session user's identity + OA groups server-side (_Users/_Groups). GxP audit trail (AuditTrail_AppSecurity) on every assignment change.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-tag-importer
title: Tag Importer
description: Tag Importer page (/tag-importer) — import device tags into WinCC OA datapoint types + datapoints from an OPC UA NodeSet2 XML file (repeated node instances of one ObjectType are mutualised into a single DPType, one DP per instance) or by browsing a live OPC UA server (a selected instance's subtree becomes the DPType). Protocol-agnostic core (intermediate model + hybrid DPType generator + address binder) with pluggable source adapters — OPC UA today, extensible to other protocols. Nested ObjectTypes shared across ≥2 parents become DPT_TYPEREF references (hybrid), one-off nesting is flattened. A dry-run preview precedes every write. Online import also writes the peripheral address configs (_address/_distrib, reference <Conn>$$1$1$<NodeId>). All engineering ops go through /api/tag-importer (WsjServerGlobal.winccoa: dpTypeCreate/dpCreate/dpSetWait + OPC UA Browse.GetBranch); no dedicated manager. Sensitive routes are role-gated server-side (Application Security roles 'browse'/'create' — open until groups are assigned).

name: @visuelconcept/wui-eng-studio
title: Engineering Studio
description: Engineering Studio page (/eng-studio) — device-first, check-in/check-out studio to model DP types, datapoints and their configs (address/alarm/archive/range) from communicating equipment. Address-book-centric imports (OPC UA browse, SimaticML/TIA Openness export, CSV, AI proposal), a live diff vs the project and a transactional, atomic check-in. Pure engineering domain in @visuelconcept/wui-eng-core (unit-tested without a runtime); all I/O behind an EngGateway (HTTP /api/eng in the shell, in-memory demo for docs/screenshots). Backend applies plans through the shared core over WsjServerGlobal.winccoa; write routes are role-gated fail-closed.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-alarms
title: Alarms
description: Alarms page (/alarms) — the plant's alarm list, live (standing alarms via the runtime AlertService) or over an archived period (alert archive), with the unacknowledged counter, the P1-P4 severity bands as a filter, the EEMUA-191 flood histogram, the recurring bad actors, free-text search, click-to-sort headers, paging and acknowledge through POST /api/alarms/ack: the webserver writes <dpe>:_alert_hdl.._ack while IMPERSONATING the session user (setUserId), so the acknowledgement is recorded under the operator's name even in projects that do not grant WebUI users the dpSet right; the route is role-gated server-side and falls back to the browser dpSet when the backend module is absent. The whole view is the shared <wui-alarm-view> component of @visuelconcept/wui-alarms-core, embeddable in any page (the Machine Fleet machine dashboard shows a machine's alarms with it, scoped to its datapoints). The priority ranges (abbreviation, colour, threshold) are the project's own: edited in the page and stored as JSON in the Alarms_Config datapoint. No manager. Application Security roles 'view'/'acknowledge'/'configure' (open until groups are assigned).

name: @visuelconcept/wui-agv-fleet
title: AGV Fleet
description: AGV Fleet page (/agv-fleet) — live read-only supervision of an automated-guided-vehicle fleet: KPI strip (fleet size, moving, available, charging, faults, average battery, utilization, missions), a sortable status list with state chips and charge bars, a warehouse floor plan showing each vehicle's live position and heading, and a detail card per vehicle. One AGV_Vehicle datapoint per vehicle, followed with one dpConnect per vehicle. The agvSim JavaScript manager drives the fleet: it dispatches real transport orders (inbound dock → rack putaway, rack → pick station → outbound dock retrieval, internal replenishment) plus battery-driven charging trips, and moves every vehicle along a guide-path graph (shortest-path routing, motion interpolated along one aisle segment at a time) so vehicles follow the aisles and never cross the racking.

name: @visuelconcept/wui-gis
title: GIS (map)
description: GIS pages (/gis + /gis/:siteid) — map-based monitoring on MapLibre GL over OpenStreetMap (BSD-3 / ODbL, no licence cost): geo-located assets bound to datapoints with live value overlays on the marker, alarm highlighting taken from the datapoint's own _alert_hdl.._act_state_color so the map agrees with the alarm list, areas (districts / sectors / catchments) as drawn polygons grouping the assets, and a configurable drill-down from map to area to asset to its process or 3D view (/fleet-3d/:atelier, /ampere/:networkid, /mosaic/:board, or the Alarms page scoped to the asset's datapoint). An asset can belong to SEVERAL areas (Asset.areaIds, a multiple-choice list in the inspector; on placement it joins every area whose outline covers the point): each of them lists and counts it, while areaIds[0] is its PRIMARY area — the only one whose badge may absorb the marker when areas collapse, since a marker is drawn once and both the draw-once and no-asset-lost-or-duplicated invariants depend on a single owner. A legacy single areaId is folded into the list on read, and the sanitiser accepts either shape. One click also FITS an area outline around the assets it lists (gis/enclose.ts): a CONCAVE outline, computed in a local metric plane, following the shape the equipment makes instead of a convex hull closed by a long chord across empty ground — which is how the first version read on a real network, as if it had joined the last asset back to the first. The hull is dug inwards chi-shape style, longest boundary edge first, through the nearest asset not yet on the boundary, as long as that keeps the polygon simple; the detour is BOUNDED rather than required to shrink, because the textbook two-shorter-edges rule cannot carve a square bay (reaching an arm’s inner corner always costs one edge longer than the chord across the mouth) and it is the pool, not the geometry, that makes it terminate. The dig threshold is measured in asset SPACINGS so one default fits a city district and a 15 km main, in a narrow band that was measured rather than guessed (1.2–3, default 1.74): a clear C has a mouth only two spacings wide, so a looser factor never digs at all — which is exactly what the first calibration did. The margin is PROPORTIONAL (8 % of the group’s diagonal, floored at 50 m and capped at 500 m) rather than a fixed 150 m that is most of a pumping station and a rounding error on a sector. The ring is the rounded OFFSET of that polygon — sides pushed out along their normals, convex corners arced, reflex corners mitred and cut past four margins — so no marker sits on the boundary, one asset gives a disc and a straight run of valves a capsule instead of a zero-area sliver with nothing to fill. Three guarantees are enforced rather than hoped for: every listed asset ends up inside; the ring never crosses itself (crossing insertions refused, the offset validated and retried at half margin, then the always-offsettable convex outline); and the ring is at most 64 points because that is what the sanitiser keeps and a truncated ring is a DIFFERENT shape — corners capped at 20, ones the margin would hide dropped first, and a hull still oversized after that (a round blob of a hundred assets) enclosed by a disc. Beyond zones the site also holds a NETWORK and information LAYERS, three concepts kept distinct on purpose: an area is GEOGRAPHY (a polygon containing assets, used for grouping and roll-ups), a CONNECTION is TOPOLOGY (a supervised link between two assets — a metro segment, a feeder, a main, a road), a ROUTE is just a NAME for a set of connections (« Ligne 1 ») and a LAYER is CLASSIFICATION (a free tag such as critical or phase-2, with no shape and no containment rule). A connection carries everything an asset carries except a position — a primary datapoint whose _alert_hdl colour PAINTS THE LINE, live readings shown on hover, a drill-down route, zone membership, layer tags, notes — because a feeder has a current and a track section has a status; without that the network would have to be drawn twice, once as geometry and once as invisible assets on top. It is deliberately NOT the same type as an asset: Asset is a point and cluster.ts grids assets in Web-Mercator world pixels, enclose.ts hulls their coordinates, assets are HTML markers while polylines must be GL layers, so paths in Site.assets would have branched every one of those and turned the no-asset-lost invariant into a statement with exceptions. Its ends are REFERENCES (from/to name assets), not coordinates, so dragging a substation drags every line attached to it with nothing recomputed — storing endpoint coordinates desynchronises the network on the first edit, which is how the feature ends up switched off; via only shapes the line between those ends. A connection whose end no longer resolves is DROPPED and counted (an invisible line is worse than none), deleting an asset cascades to its connections, and a self-connection goes the same way. A metro line is NOT one object: the tempting Route{stops[]} with segments implied between consecutive stops breaks the first time a station is inserted, because every later segment shifts by one and so does every datapoint binding attached by index — a silent mis-binding. Segments are therefore explicit objects with stable ids (also physically right: a fault occurs BETWEEN two stations), and a route does not list its stops at all — the order is DERIVED by walking the from/to chain, and a branching line (one plant feeding three reservoirs) returns null rather than an invented sequence. The line tool draws a whole line in one continuous gesture: click assets one after another, each click closing a segment and opening the next, clicks on the map between two assets adding shaping points, and the route picker creating the line on the spot (New line…) so nobody has to fill a form before they can draw. Rendering is three GL layers — an invisible fat hit line (a 3.5 px track is unclickable otherwise), a dark casing that keeps a coloured route legible over a raster basemap, then the dashed-by-kind line — below the area outlines, above nothing, needing no glyphs. Connections are never clustered: lines do not collide like discs, so they stay drawn at every zoom and a faulted feeder is visible even when its zone has collapsed to a badge. Layers are tags with a BROWSER: create, rename, recolour, delete, per-layer visibility, isolate-one, plus a usage count; a tag can also be created straight from an asset by typing a name into its editable Layers field, because the need for a tag is discovered while looking at the asset, not before. Layer VISIBILITY IS NOT STORED — which layers an operator is looking at is a property of the operator, so it is session state (and therefore usable without the edit grant); an untagged object is never hidden and a tagged one survives while at least one of its tags is on. Selecting an asset shows chips for its zones, layers and lines at the top of its panel, and each chip NAVIGATES — a zone chip goes to the zone, a line chip opens its segment. Selecting an area fills the side panel with one card per asset showing that asset live values, alarm-edged when it is in alarm and clickable to open the asset. Stored as GIS_Site DPs, one per site; the overview doubles as the multi-site view with a live in-alarm count per site. Basemap is per site: public OSM tiles, an own XYZ raster server, an own MapLibre vector style, or none at all for an air-gapped plant (assets and areas still draw). Zoomed out the markers group as a three-rung hierarchy — assets, then one badge per area (ringed in the area colour, so it says which zone is in trouble), then one badge for the whole site — on by default and toggled off to draw everything. A badge is a FAULT SYNTHESIS and nothing else: it draws only the number of its assets in alarm, and a group with no alarm is NOT DRAWN AT ALL — zoomed out the map is zones plus trouble, the area polygons saying where the equipment is and a bubble appearing only where something is wrong, so a quiet plant is a quiet map and anything visible on it is something to go and look at. A bubble with nothing to synthesise was still an object the eye had to check and discard, which is the opposite of what a synthesis is for; the member count stays in the badge tooltip. The drop happens in the VIEW rather than by removing quiet groups from the grouping, so "no asset lost or duplicated" stays a testable statement about cluster.ts — with the known consequence that quiet assets folded into a flat-grid cell are absent until you zoom in, there being no polygon to stand in for a grid cell the way there is for an area. An alarmed asset is therefore grouped like any other rather than escaping every badge — it is not hidden, the badge turns alarm-coloured and states how many it swallowed, and one click zooms to exactly those assets, whereas keeping alarms out turned a plant in trouble seen from far out into the very pile of loose discs grouping exists to prevent. The collapse threshold is configurable per area and per site, defaulting to automatic: an area collapses when its extent no longer fits its assets, and the site threshold is DERIVED from the area ones (1.5 zoom levels below the last expanded area, bounded by area-badge overlap) because independent pixel thresholds put both collapses inside one integer zoom step and the area rung would never be seen. An area is always grouped WHOLE or not at all — never a few loose markers plus an anonymous badge holding the rest of the same area: the collapse is measured on the area assets rather than on its ring, on a raw (unpadded) extent, and in automatic mode an area also collapses whenever the flat grid would merge any two of its assets. The grid is anchored in Web Mercator world pixels so panning never re-buckets anything; clicking a badge zooms into exactly its members. In-place edit mode places and drags markers, draws and RESHAPES area outlines (corner handles to drag or click-to-remove, hollow midpoint handles to click-to-insert, a triangle being the protected floor; the drag is buffered in the map component and handed to the page on dragend) and binds datapoints. Asset name plates are drawn only for a disc that is visually on its own (nearest-neighbour distance in world pixels), so a busy map never turns into overlapping text. An AREA is never labelled on the map: its name appears in a tooltip following the cursor while the pointer is over its outline, naming every zone under the cursor since zones may overlap — a dozen permanent plates competing with the asset plates for the same pixels is unreadable, and the polygon and its colour already say where a zone is. Embeds a proposal-only AI assistant (toolless, via the optional /api/ai bridge, hidden unless the deploy enables it and the user holds the edit role) that drafts a whole site — areas and assets, with suggested readings but never a datapoint binding — for review on the map before saving; every proposal is coerced through a sanitiser that drops unusable positions, unknown kinds, dangling area references and off-site links, and caps a runaway answer (64 areas and 10 000 assets per site) — a ceiling against a runaway answer rather than a capacity claim, since three real limits sit below it and did not move when it was raised: one dpConnect per datapoint element (deliberately isolated, so ~30 000 subscriptions at that size), one HTML marker per drawn asset, and the whole site JSON in one WinCC OA String element. Falls back to two demo sites (water network, smart-city district) when the project has no GIS_Site datapoint. Import/export in two formats: native JSON ({kind:gis-sites,version,sites}, all sites or one) round-tripping bindings, readings, drill-down routes, basemap and grouping thresholds; and GeoJSON per site (areas as Polygon, assets as Point, connections as LineString carrying their from/to so the topology is rebuilt rather than frozen, routes and layers as collection metadata since they have no geometry) for QGIS/ArcGIS interop — which is also how surveyed coordinates come back in, correcting the assistant's approximate ones. A native import creates sites, a GeoJSON import fills the open site through the same review-then-Done path the assistant uses, and a FOREIGN layer with no gisType property is read by geometry (polygon=area, point=asset). Every import passes through the same sanitiser as an AI proposal. Frontend only — no backend route, no manager; maplibre-gl (pinned to 5.x in tools/external-dependencies.mjs) is auto-detected from the vendored page and bundled into it.
